---
title: "Gated annotations"
---

The UDS event protocol uses the natural-parts response as a gate. A yes displays questions about part similarity and average part duration; a no displays questions about whole-situation duration and dynamicity. An undisplayed response is thus a **by-design absence**. It is not a low value on that branch and not a failed attempt to answer a displayed question.

The local extract supports numerical analysis of the [observed natural-parts gate](uds-measurement-model.qmd) only. It does not contain audited raw conditional-branch responses, and the available raw confidence serialization conflicts with the documented response scale. This page thus analyzes the gate empirically and keeps the branch model symbolic.

## Reproducing the observed gate

```{r}
#| label: load-uds-gate
#| message: false
#| warning: false

uds <- utils::read.csv(
  "data/uds/uds-natural-parts.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
uds_cache <- readRDS(
  "data/uds/uds-natural-parts-teaching-cache.rds"
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(uds) == 2955L,
  sum(uds$natural_parts) == 659L,
  setequal(unique(uds$natural_parts), 0:1),
  nrow(uds_cache$population_draws) == 400L,
  identical(uds_cache$item_levels, unique(uds$item_id)),
  identical(uds_cache$annotator_levels, unique(uds$annotator_id))
)

uds$item_index <- match(uds$item_id, uds_cache$item_levels)
uds$annotator_index <- match(
  uds$annotator_id,
  uds_cache$annotator_levels
)

gate_summary <- data.frame(
  response = c("No", "Yes"),
  count = c(
    sum(uds$natural_parts == 0L),
    sum(uds$natural_parts == 1L)
  ),
  proportion = c(
    mean(uds$natural_parts == 0L),
    mean(uds$natural_parts == 1L)
  )
)

knitr::kable(gate_summary, digits = 3)
```

These are recorded gate responses. The no count is not a count of zero-valued part-similarity judgments, because the part-similarity question was never displayed after those responses.

## Factoring the gate and follow-up response

Let $G_{ij}=1$ when annotator $j$ reports that predicate-node item $i$ has natural parts, and let $G_{ij}=0$ otherwise. Let $Y_{ij}$ denote a response on the yes branch, such as part similarity. Write $\pi_{ij}$ for the gate probability and $f_Y(y_{ij}\mid\phi_{ij})$ for the conditional follow-up probability or density.

The observed response contribution is

$$
f_{G,Y}(g_{ij},y_{ij}^{\mathrm{obs}})
=
\begin{cases}
\pi_{ij}f_Y(y_{ij}\mid\phi_{ij}), & g_{ij}=1,\\
1-\pi_{ij}, & g_{ij}=0.
\end{cases}
$$

When $g_{ij}=1$, the record contributes a gate factor and a follow-up factor. When $g_{ij}=0$, it contributes only the negative-gate probability. The second case never evaluates a density at an unrecorded follow-up value.

The same factorization can be written as

$$
f_{G,Y}(g_{ij},y_{ij}^{\mathrm{obs}})
=
\left[\pi_{ij}f_Y(y_{ij}\mid\phi_{ij})\right]^{g_{ij}}
(1-\pi_{ij})^{1-g_{ij}},
$$

where the follow-up term is meaningful only for records on which the branch is observed. This expression describes a future branch-bearing analysis; it is not evaluated on the present extract.

## Checking only the fitted gate

The following posterior predictive calculation uses the audited binary gate model. It simulates no follow-up values.

```{r}
#| label: compute-uds-gate-ppc

set.seed(20261103L)
gate_ppc <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(uds_cache$population_draws)),
  function(draw) {
    eta <-
      uds_cache$population_draws[draw, "alpha"] +
      uds_cache$item_effect_draws[draw, uds$item_index] +
      uds_cache$annotator_effect_draws[draw, uds$annotator_index]
    mean(stats::rbinom(
      nrow(uds),
      size = 1,
      prob = stats::plogis(eta)
    ))
  },
  numeric(1)
)
observed_gate_rate <- mean(uds$natural_parts)
gate_interval <- stats::quantile(
  gate_ppc,
  c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975) # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
)

stopifnot(
  observed_gate_rate >= gate_interval[[1]],
  observed_gate_rate <= gate_interval[[3]]
)

data.frame(
  observed = observed_gate_rate,
  predictive_lower = gate_interval[[1]],
  predictive_median = gate_interval[[2]],
  predictive_upper = gate_interval[[3]]
)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-uds-gate-ppc
#| fig-width: 5.8
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive distribution of the observed natural-parts gate rate. The vertical line marks the released rate."

ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(gate_rate = gate_ppc), ggplot2::aes(gate_rate)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(
    bins = 25,
    fill = "grey75",
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = observed_gate_rate,
    color = "#2B6F8A",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Replicated natural-parts yes rate",
    y = "Draws"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

This check supports the gate component at the overall-rate level. It supplies no evidence about the conditional branches because no branch response was simulated or scored.

## The follow-up target is conditional

An average of observed yes-branch responses would describe cases that passed the gate:

$$
\mathbb{E}[Y_{ij}\mid G_{ij}=1].
$$

It would not estimate an unconditional property over all predicate nodes unless the model defined what the follow-up means when an annotator rejects the premise that natural parts exist. Replacing an undisplayed part-similarity response with zero would merge two events: rejecting the gate and passing the gate while selecting the scale's lowest response.

The gate and a future follow-up model might share item or annotator quantities. For instance, an item that often passes the gate might also tend to receive a particular conditional response. But such dependence requires raw branch-bearing records, enough passed gates, a reconciled response scale, and a new recovery study. The present gate fit cannot identify it.

## Separating protocol absence from stochastic missingness

A rectangular data table may store `NA` for an undisplayed follow-up. The joint model, not the storage symbol, determines what that `NA` means. Protocol absence differs from the missing intended measurements discussed in [missingness mechanisms](../missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd): here the instrument defines no follow-up response after the incompatible gate value.

The blocked measurements are part similarity, part duration, whole-situation duration, dynamicity, and raw confidence. No numerical claim about their distributions, associations, or fitted values follows from this page.

::: {.callout-note title="Check the gate"}
1. Which factor contributes when $g_{ij}=0$?
2. What population does $\mathbb{E}[Y_{ij}\mid G_{ij}=1]$ describe?
3. Why is a protocol-generated blank different from a recorded zero?
4. What does the gate-rate predictive check leave untested?
5. What evidence would a branch model require?
:::

A gated likelihood gives negative gates one gate factor and affirmative gates both a gate factor and a conditional follow-up factor. The observed UDS extract supports the first component only. Keeping the second component symbolic preserves the logic of the instrument without inventing data.
